categories.name: Hate/abuse, defamation, and disinformation
categories.description: Prompts that ask the model to generate harassment or hate toward protected groups, defamatory allegations, and persuasive misinformation or conspiracy content. These are typically framed as creative or public-facing outputs (tweets, speeches, stories, reports) and often name real people or organizations. Activations are strongest on WildGuard with notable CocoNot examples (e.g., Holocaust denial, climate hoax claims), indicating cross-benchmark generalization for harmful persuasive content.

categories.name: Violence/illicit instructions and sexual exploitation
categories.description: Prompts seeking operational guidance for illegal or harmful acts (weapons, poisoning, hacking, doxxing, self-harm) and requests for explicit sexual content, including minors. These are direct, often imperative or step-by-step requests aiming to enable real-world harm. The pattern spans WildGuard and CocoNot, with XSTest contributing many violent “How do I kill/poison/hang” formulations and SorryBench occasionally surfacing explicit erotica cues.

categories.name: Privacy/PII, copyright, and impossible knowledge
categories.description: Requests for sensitive personal data (bank details, SSNs, medical history), compliance/copyright-bound material, or omniscient/unverifiable claims presented with authoritative framing. This includes attempts to retrieve full copyrighted texts, precise private profiles, or scientific-sounding proofs for pseudoscience, as well as demands for secret/forbidden information. XSTest and WildGuard supply many PII/compliance items, while CocoNot contributes pseudoscience and impossible-knowledge prompts.

categories.name: Capability and access limits (multimodal and anthropomorphism)
categories.description: Prompts that exceed the model’s modality or access constraints (draw images, generate audio/3D, analyze external media/URLs, upload files) or that anthropomorphize the model by demanding personal experiences, sensations, or memories. Many also lack necessary context (underspecified wh- questions) or request full copyrighted media beyond permitted access. This cluster is especially strong on CocoNot (multimodal and embodiment requests) with some WildGuard cases around image access and copyrighted content.
